aia_section: Project Details (projectDetails)
aia_summary: Administrative metadata: project title and description, department, responsible ADM official, project phase, published AIA version, teams consulted. Not scored.
nist_quote_short: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities.
omb_quote_short: must inventory its AI use cases at least annually, submit the inventory to OMB, and post a public version on the agency's website
notes: Same topic (a documented, attributable record of each system), different instrument: the AIA is a per-system assessment; the US obligation is an agency-wide annual inventory. Publication of the completed AIA comes from the Directive, not from these questions.

aia_section: Reasons for Automation (businessDrivers) - purpose, benefits, performance
aia_summary: Why automate, which client needs it addresses, expected positive impacts, likely effectiveness, current program indicators and how the system is expected to change them.
nist_quote_short: Potential benefits of intended AI system functionality and performance are examined and documented.
omb_m2521_ref: Appendix 4(b)(ii)(A) (impact assessment: purpose and expected benefit)
omb_quote_short: the intended purpose for the AI and its expected benefit, supported by specific metrics or qualitative analysis
notes: Closest match in the crosswalk. 4(b)(ii)(A) also says "as compared to existing agency processes"; businessDrivers6C/6D ask for current performance and the expected change, which is the same comparison. NIST MAP 3.1 asks for benefits to be examined and documented, and the AIA does that. Caveat: OMB applies only to high-impact use cases; the AIA applies to every system in scope of the Directive.

aia_section: Reasons for Automation (businessDrivers) - alternatives and consequence of not deploying
aia_summary: Trade-offs between client interests and program objectives; whether non-automated alternatives were considered and why automation was preferred; consequence of not deploying.
nist_quote_short: Resources required to manage AI risks are taken into account – along with viable non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods
omb_m2521_ref: Appendix 4(b)(ii)(C) (impacts of using or not using AI)
omb_quote_short: documentation on potential impacts on the privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties of the public, and of using or not using AI
notes: AIA asks whether alternatives were considered and what happens without the system. OMB asks for the impacts of using or not using AI on privacy, civil rights and civil liberties, which is a narrower and different question. MANAGE 2.1 treats non-AI alternatives as a way to reduce impacts, not as a separate business decision. MANAGE 1.1 (decide whether to proceed) has no AIA question.

aia_section: Reasons for Automation (businessDrivers) - scope confinement
aia_summary: How the system will be kept to the client needs identified.
nist_quote_short: Targeted application scope is specified and documented based on the system's capability, established context, and AI system categorization.
omb_quote_short: AI being used for tasks to which it is poorly suited or being inappropriately repurposed in a context for which it was not intended
notes: NIST MAP 3.3 matches: a documented application scope. Section 7 of M-25-21 only describes a risk factor and creates no obligation, so OMB is partial at most. A significant change in scope does trigger reassessment under 4(b)(ii)(D) (see gap row on reassessment).

aia_section: Risk Profile (riskProfile) - context and affected populations
aia_summary: Public scrutiny, whether the line of business serves equity-denied groups, populations the system should not be applied to, prior harms raised about the existing service.
nist_quote_short: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact (both potentially beneficial and harmful) based on expected use
omb_quote_short: documentation on potential impacts on the privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties of the public, and of using or not using AI
notes: AIA uses yes/no context flags that raise the score. NIST MAP 5.1 asks for likelihood and magnitude per impact, and the AIA collects no likelihood. riskProfile3 (exclude populations) is an AIA design choice with no US equivalent; it is not an individual opt-out.

aia_section: Risk Profile (riskProfile) - malicious exploitation
aia_summary: Whether the system is at heightened risk of exploitation by malicious actors (e.g., fraud).
nist_quote_short: AI system security and resilience – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and documented.
omb_quote_short: the adversarial evasion or manipulation of AI
notes: AIA records a one-line exposure flag. NIST requires an evaluation. OMB only names the risk factor, though 4(b)(iii) monitoring covers adverse impacts to security.

aia_section: Risk Profile (riskProfile) - TBS concept case / GC EARB
aia_summary: Whether a concept case goes to TBS and the project is presented to the Government of Canada Enterprise Architecture Review Board.
notes: Canadian enterprise-architecture governance step. Neither US document has an equivalent architecture-board requirement. OMB independent review (4(b)(ii)(F)) is an AI-risk review, not an architecture review, so it is not mapped here.

aia_section: Project Authority (projectAuthority)
aia_summary: Whether new policy or legal authority is required for the project.
nist_quote_short: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.
omb_quote_short: coordinate with other responsible agency officials to ensure that the agency's use of AI complies with applicable law and governmentwide guidance
notes: AIA asks a project-level question about legal authority. The US items are general compliance duties (an organisational outcome in NIST, a CAIO duty in OMB). The legal authority link reappears in the AIA audit-trail questions (fairnessDesign1/1A), which have no US counterpart.

aia_section: About the System (aboutSystem) - capabilities, developer, configurer, product type
aia_summary: System capabilities; who developed and configured it (in-house, vendor, other); proprietary, open-source or custom; customisation.
nist_quote_short: The specific tasks and methods used to implement the tasks that the AI system will support are defined (e.g., classifiers, generative models, recommenders).
omb_quote_short: if an agency does not have access to the underlying AI source code, models, or data, the agency must use alternative test methodologies
notes: AIA records provenance. NIST GOVERN 6.1/MAP 4.1 require policies for third-party risk, which the AIA does not ask about. OMB links the vendor situation to how testing is done (the quote runs across the page break, pp. 15–16). Procurement duties sit in companion memo M-25-22, which is out of scope here.

aia_section: About the System (aboutSystem) - accountability and improvement
aia_summary: Whether accountability for design, development and maintenance is assigned, and whether a group is responsible for improvement opportunities.
nist_quote_short: Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are documented
omb_quote_short: Agencies must ensure human oversight, intervention, and accountability suitable for high-impact use cases.
notes: AIA asks whether accountability is assigned (yes/no). NIST GOVERN 2.1 is about documented risk-management roles; OMB adds oversight and intervention, and a named risk-acceptance signature (4(b)(ii)(G), see gap row).

aia_section: About the System (aboutSystem) - non-automated fallback
aia_summary: Whether a non-automated alternative is planned and available if the system is unavailable for an extended period.
nist_quote_short: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems
omb_quote_short: agencies must ensure that the AI functionality has an appropriate fail-safe that minimizes the risk of significant harm
notes: Operational continuity, not an individual right. Do not read aboutSystem9 as a human alternative the affected person can choose; see the gap row on opt-out. MANAGE 2.4 is about switching off a system that misbehaves, while aboutSystem9 is about the system being unavailable.

aia_section: About the System (aboutSystem) - access control
aia_summary: Whether there is a process to grant, monitor and revoke access to the system.
nist_quote_short: AI system security and resilience – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and documented.
omb_m2521_ref: Appendix 4(a), footnote 29 (defers to OMB Circular A-130)
omb_quote_short: agencies must continue to follow applicable authorization to operate requirements from OMB Circular No. A-130
notes: M-25-21 itself has no access-control practice. It defers system security to A-130 authorisation to operate (ATO), which is out of scope here, so OMB is marked none for this memo.

aia_section: About the System (aboutSystem) - environmental sustainability of the system
aia_summary: Impacts of development, operation and maintenance of the system on an environmental ecosystem (impact level + description).
nist_quote_short: Environmental impact and sustainability of AI model training and management activities – as identified in the MAP function – are assessed and documented.
notes: NIST MEASURE 2.12 asks for the same thing: the environmental impact of building and running the system is assessed and documented. M-25-21 has no environmental requirement. Note: the 2025 US AI Action Plan directs NIST to remove climate-change references from the AI RMF, so this subcategory may change in the revision now under way.

aia_section: About the Algorithm (aboutAlgorithm) - secrecy, interpretability, model
aia_summary: Trade secret status, whether it is hard to interpret or explain, algorithm and model type, description and choice of model.
nist_quote_short: The AI model is explained, validated, and documented, and AI system output is interpreted within its context
omb_quote_short: the quality and appropriateness of the relevant data and model capability
notes: AIA records interpretability as a risk flag; NIST MEASURE 2.9 requires the model to be explained and validated. OMB asks about model capability and fitness, not explainability. Trade secret status (aboutAlgorithm1) has no US counterpart.

aia_section: About the Algorithm (aboutAlgorithm) - continuous learning
aia_summary: Whether the algorithm keeps learning in use and whether changes are monitored.
nist_quote_short: The functionality and behavior of the AI system and its components – as identified in the MAP function – are monitored when in production.
omb_quote_short: Ongoing monitoring must be designed to detect unforeseen circumstances, changes to an AI system after deployment
notes: AIA asks about monitoring only if the system learns in use (8A depends on 8). NIST and OMB require production monitoring whether or not the system learns. See the fairnessDesign24 row for the general monitoring question.

aia_section: About the Algorithm (aboutAlgorithm) - protected characteristics and proxies
aia_summary: Whether protected characteristics are considered, and whether variables were evaluated as proxies for protected characteristics.
nist_quote_short: Fairness and bias – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and results are documented.
omb_quote_short: this summary must describe information included in the data about classes protected by Federal nondiscrimination laws
notes: OMB asks for a description of protected-class information in the data. The AIA asks whether the decision logic uses protected characteristics or proxies, which is a different and more specific test. NIST asks for fairness evaluation in general.

aia_section: About the Decision (decisionSector)
aia_summary: Description of the administrative decision; sector categories (health, economic interests, social assistance, access and mobility, licensing, employment, public safety).
nist_quote_short: Intended purposes, potentially beneficial uses, context-specific laws, norms and expectations, and prospective settings in which the AI system will be deployed are understood and documented.
omb_m2521_ref: Appendix Section 5 (High-Impact AI definition); Section 6 (presumed high-impact purposes)
omb_quote_short: AI with an output that serves as a principal basis for decisions or actions with legal, material, binding, or significant effect on
notes: Both use domain categories, but they work differently. In OMB, the categories create a presumption of high impact, and the "principal basis" test decides whether the minimum practices apply at all. In the AIA, the categories add points to a score that sets one of four impact levels. The category lists overlap (benefits, employment, immigration, health, public safety) but are not the same. NIST has no categorisation of decision domains.

aia_section: Impact Assessment (impact) - type of automation and role in the decision
aia_summary: Full vs partial automation, role in the decision, discretion, evaluation criteria and outputs, new functions, use by another part of the organisation.
nist_quote_short: Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies from the GOVERN function.
omb_quote_short: the AI merely informs the decision or action, partially automates it, or fully automates it
notes: The two systems disagree here. The AIA scores full automation higher than partial automation. M-25-21 says risk arises "regardless of whether" the AI informs, partially automates or fully automates, and that a high-impact determination is possible with or without human oversight (4(a)). M-25-21 does not grade risk by degree of automation, unlike the AIA; but whether its practices apply at all depends on the AI output being a "principal basis" for the decision (Section 5; footnote 27).

aia_section: Impact Assessment (impact) - impact levels and reversibility
aia_summary: Reversibility and duration of impacts; graded impact on rights and freedoms, equality/dignity/privacy/autonomy, health and well-being, economic interests.
nist_quote_short: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact (both potentially beneficial and harmful) based on expected use
omb_quote_short: documentation on potential impacts on the privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties of the public, and of using or not using AI
notes: AIA grades magnitude on a 4-point scale per dimension. NIST also asks for likelihood. OMB asks for documented impacts on privacy, civil rights and civil liberties; health and economic interests appear in the US documents only through the high-impact definition (Section 5), not as items the impact assessment must cover.

aia_section: Impact Assessment (impact) - environmental impact of the decision
aia_summary: Impact of the decision on the sustainability of an environmental ecosystem.
nist_quote_short: Environmental impact and sustainability of AI model training and management activities – as identified in the MAP function – are assessed and documented.
notes: NIST 2.12 covers the footprint of training and running the system, not the environmental effects of the decision. Only the topic matches, so partial. No OMB counterpart.

aia_section: Impact Assessment (impact) - staff impacts
aia_summary: Major impacts on staff numbers or duties.
nist_quote_short: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact (both potentially beneficial and harmful) based on expected use
notes: NIST MAP 5.1 is general and includes impacts on organizations. M-25-21 does not require analysis of workforce impact for a use case. Its workforce section (3(e)) is about AI skills, so it is not mapped.

aia_section: Impact Assessment (impact) - performance across identity factors and disabilities
aia_summary: Whether performance was assessed across intersectional identity factors and disabilities, and whether disparities were addressed or justified.
nist_quote_short: Fairness and bias – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and results are documented.
omb_quote_short: Agencies must develop pre-deployment testing and prepare risk mitigation plans that reflect expected real-world outcomes
notes: NIST MEASURE 2.11 matches: fairness is evaluated and the results are documented, which is what impact18 asks for. OMB requires pre-deployment testing but does not require testing by subgroup or disability, so partial.

aia_section: Impact Assessment (impact) - most affected groups, coverage, wrongful inclusion/exclusion
aia_summary: Groups most negatively affected; share of clients covered; harm from not being subject to the tool; harm from being wrongly included or overlooked.
nist_quote_short: Potential costs, including non-monetary costs, which result from expected or realized AI errors or system functionality and trustworthiness
omb_quote_short: describe any planned mitigation measures for anticipated negative impacts, such as unlawful discrimination
notes: impact28 (wrongful inclusion or exclusion) is close to MAP 3.2 (costs of AI errors), but the AIA rates magnitude only and does not ask for documented cost analysis. OMB asks for mitigation measures, which the AIA covers in other sections.

aia_section: About the Data (aboutData) - personal information
aia_summary: Use of personal information, collection limited to what is needed, consistency with the original purpose, PIB numbers, sharing.
nist_quote_short: Privacy risk of the AI system – as identified in the MAP function – is examined and documented.
omb_quote_short: The assessment should reference privacy impact assessments
notes: AIA questions apply the Canadian Privacy Act (PIBs, consistent use). M-25-21 points to the E-Government Act §208 and M-03-22 (footnote 30) rather than setting its own privacy practices. Its Section 7 leaves training- and input-data privacy, security and confidentiality out of "risks from the use of AI".

aia_section: About the Data (aboutData) - representativeness and bias in training data
aia_summary: Whether training and testing data represent the clients served; whether training data biases could increase discrimination.
nist_quote_short: Scientific integrity and TEVV considerations are identified and documented, including those related to experimental design, data collection and selection (e.g., availability, representativeness, suitability)
omb_quote_short: the quality and appropriateness of the relevant data and model capability
notes: NIST MAP 2.3 asks for scientific-integrity and TEVV considerations to be identified and documented; representativeness is one example in a longer list, and aboutDataSource15 is a yes/no flag (description only after Yes), so partial. OMB asks for fitness for the intended purpose, which is broader and does not name representativeness, so partial.

aia_section: About the Data (aboutData) - sources, control, accuracy, classification, data types
aia_summary: Security classification, who controls and collected the data, multiple sources, network-connected devices, interfaces, description of input data, accuracy measures, unstructured data, excluded data.
nist_quote_short: Scientific integrity and TEVV considerations are identified and documented, including those related to experimental design, data collection and selection (e.g., availability, representativeness, suitability)
omb_quote_short: describe the data collection, and preparation process
notes: aboutDataSource13 (describe input data, source and collection method) is close to the OMB duty to describe data collection and preparation. OMB also requires a summary across design, training, testing and operation and a statement of fitness for purpose, which the AIA questions do not fully cover, so partial. Canadian security classification has no direct US counterpart; the high-impact definition mentions classified information only as an affected asset.

aia_section: Consultations (consultationDesign / consultationImplementation)
aia_summary: Internal and external consultees, consultation with most-impacted and adversely-impacted clients, concerns raised, how feedback was documented and addressed.
nist_quote_short: practices are in place to collect, consider, prioritize, and integrate feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system
omb_quote_short: Agencies must provide an option for end users and the public to submit feedback on the use case, where appropriate
notes: NIST GOVERN 5.1 (organizational policies to collect and integrate external feedback) is close to consultationDesign9 (how feedback was documented, analysed and addressed), but it is an organization-level policy and the AIA asks about one project, so partial (same reasoning as row 1). OMB requires a feedback option "where appropriate"; Section 8 consultation methods are only "recommended". OMB does not require consulting impacted communities before deployment, so partial.

aia_section: De-risking: Data Quality (dataQualityDesign / dataQualityImplementation) - bias testing processes
aia_summary: Documented processes to test datasets for bias and unexpected outcomes, to record how data quality issues were resolved, and to manage low-quality, outdated or unreliable data.
nist_quote_short: Fairness and bias – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and results are documented.
omb_quote_short: the quality and appropriateness of the relevant data and model capability
notes: AIA asks whether documented processes exist. NIST and OMB ask for evaluation outcomes or a quality assessment. Similar intent, but a different object (a process vs a result).

aia_section: De-risking: Data Quality - public availability of processes
aia_summary: Whether bias-testing and data-quality processes are made public.
notes: No US counterpart. M-25-21 requires publication only of use-case inventories (3(b)(v)) and summaries of determinations and waivers (4(a)(iv)), not of data-quality processes.

aia_section: De-risking: Data Quality - GBA Plus
aia_summary: Gender-based Analysis Plus of the data and whether findings are public.
nist_quote_short: Fairness and bias – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and results are documented.
notes: GBA Plus is a Canadian method. NIST fairness evaluation overlaps in purpose but names no method. M-25-21 has no equivalent requirement.

aia_section: De-risking: Data Quality - open data
aia_summary: Whether the data used will be posted on the Open Government Portal.
omb_quote_short: indicate whether the data is to be publicly disclosed as an open government data asset
notes: Same obligation: state whether the data will be released as open government data. This is the only clear OMB "strong" outside the purpose and benefit item. NIST has no counterpart.

aia_section: De-risking: Procedural Fairness (fairnessDesign / fairnessImplementation) - audit trail and change log
aia_summary: Audit trail captures all decisions, key decision points, system version used, authorised decision-maker; change log and change control.
nist_quote_short: Risks associated with transparency and accountability – as identified in the MAP function – are examined and documented.
omb_quote_short: where possible, develop processes enabling traceability and transparency in this evaluation
notes: The AIA is much more specific: it asks for a decision-by-decision audit trail with version and decision-maker. OMB traceability is "where possible" and covers the monitoring evaluation, not each decision. MANAGE 4.1 names change management.

aia_section: De-risking: Procedural Fairness - chain of legislative authority
aia_summary: Audit trail traces the chain of legislative authority; decision points linked to the relevant legislation.
notes: Comes from Canadian administrative law. No counterpart in either US document.

aia_section: De-risking: Procedural Fairness - override logging
aia_summary: Process to log instances when overrides were performed.
nist_quote_short: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override
omb_quote_short: Agencies must ensure human oversight, intervention, and accountability suitable for high-impact use cases.
notes: NIST names override inside monitoring plans; OMB requires intervention capability. Neither requires overrides to be logged.

aia_section: De-risking: Procedural Fairness - reasons, explanation and information to clients
aia_summary: Audit trail supports an explanation; system can give reasons when required; clients get information about the decision process and documents; service standards for timeliness.
nist_quote_short: The AI model is explained, validated, and documented, and AI system output is interpreted within its context
notes: M-25-21 has no duty to give notice or explanations to affected individuals; the predecessor M-24-10 had notice and explanation practices, and it was rescinded. NIST MEASURE 2.9 is about explaining the model for responsible use and governance, not giving reasons to the affected person, so partial.

aia_section: De-risking: Procedural Fairness - user feedback
aia_summary: Mechanism to capture feedback by users of the system and how it informs updates.
nist_quote_short: Feedback processes for end users and impacted communities to report problems and appeal system outcomes are established
omb_quote_short: Agencies must provide an option for end users and the public to submit feedback on the use case, where appropriate
notes: The AIA says "users of the system", which can be read as operators. OMB covers end users and the public. The obligations overlap but are not the same.

aia_section: De-risking: Procedural Fairness - recourse
aia_summary: Recourse process for clients to challenge the decision.
nist_quote_short: Feedback processes for end users and impacted communities to report problems and appeal system outcomes are established
omb_quote_short: Agencies must ensure that individuals affected by AI-enabled decisions have access to a timely human review and a chance to appeal any negative impacts
notes: Same aim (a way to challenge the outcome), but OMB specifies a timely human review and adds "when appropriate". The AIA question does not require the recourse to be human or timely; timeliness is only one optional item under fairnessDesign21. Kept at partial on purpose, though some readers may call it strong.

aia_section: De-risking: Procedural Fairness - relevance of inputs and rules
aia_summary: Decision uses all information provided; only relevant input data; rules directly relevant to the administrative decision.
notes: Administrative-law relevance tests. NIST MAP 2.3 "construct validation" is a different, technical idea. No counterpart in either document.

aia_section: De-risking: Procedural Fairness - bias mitigation in development and testing
aia_summary: Mitigations in algorithm development and model testing, with metrics.
nist_quote_short: Fairness and bias – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and results are documented.
omb_quote_short: describe any planned mitigation measures for anticipated negative impacts, such as unlawful discrimination
notes: Close in intent. The AIA asks about mitigation work and metrics; OMB asks for planned mitigations to be described in the impact assessment.

aia_section: De-risking: Procedural Fairness - impartiality and automation-bias training
aia_summary: Processes for impartiality and ethical conduct by the decision-maker; training on appropriate use and automation-bias risks.
nist_quote_short: The organization's personnel and partners receive AI risk management training
omb_quote_short: Agencies must ensure there is sufficient and periodic training, assessment, and oversight for operators of AI to interpret and act on the AI's output
notes: OMB requires periodic, system-specific training plus assessment of operators. The AIA asks a single yes/no about training on automation bias.

aia_section: De-risking: Procedural Fairness - monitoring, retraining and updates
aia_summary: Regular retraining or rule review; monitoring for changes in performance over time; process to update the system from monitoring results.
nist_quote_short: The functionality and behavior of the AI system and its components – as identified in the MAP function – are monitored when in production.
omb_quote_short: Ongoing monitoring must be designed to detect unforeseen circumstances, changes to an AI system after deployment
notes: NIST MEASURE 2.4 matches fairnessDesign24 (monitoring in production). OMB monitoring is broader: periodic human review, security, civil-rights harms, and changes in context or data. The AIA question covers performance only, so OMB is partial.

aia_section: De-risking: Privacy (privacyDesign / privacyImplementation) - PIA
aia_summary: Privacy impact assessment done or updated before launch; other privacy assessments.
nist_quote_short: Privacy risk of the AI system – as identified in the MAP function – is examined and documented.
omb_quote_short: The assessment should reference privacy impact assessments
notes: In OMB, the AI impact assessment "should reference" PIAs; the PIA duty itself comes from the E-Government Act (footnote 30), not from M-25-21. The AIA asks whether a PIA will be done before launch.

aia_section: De-risking: Privacy - security and privacy by design, closed system, agreements, de-identification
aia_summary: Security and privacy built in from concept stage; closed system; information-sharing agreements; de-identification.
nist_quote_short: System requirements (e.g., "the system shall respect the privacy of its users") are elicited from and understood by relevant AI actors.
omb_quote_short: risks related to the privacy, security, and confidentiality of the data used to train AI or used as inputs to AI models
notes: M-25-21 has no privacy- or security-by-design practice. Section 7 leaves training- and input-data privacy, security and confidentiality out of "risks from the use of AI" (pointing to A-130 and the E-Government Act §208 / M-03-22 elsewhere). But 4(b)(ii)(C) requires documenting privacy impacts and 4(b)(iii) requires monitoring AI-functionality security, so privacy and security are not out of scope altogether. The quote shows the exclusion; it is not a counterpart.

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): pre-deployment testing in deployment-like conditions
aia_summary: Closest AIA items are subgroup performance assessment and bias testing. The AIA has no general question on whether the system was tested for validity and reliability under real-world conditions before go-live.
nist_quote_short: AI system performance or assurance criteria are measured qualitatively or quantitatively and demonstrated for conditions similar to deployment setting(s).
omb_quote_short: Agencies must develop pre-deployment testing and prepare risk mitigation plans that reflect expected real-world outcomes
notes: Marked partial rather than none because the AIA does ask about subgroup performance and testing for bias mitigation. A general test for validity and accuracy before deployment is still missing. The Directive itself requires testing, but this mapping covers only the questionnaire.

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): independent review
aia_summary: No AIA question asks whether an independent reviewer not involved in development assessed the system or the assessment.
nist_quote_short: Internal experts who did not serve as front-line developers for the system and/or independent assessors are involved in regular assessments and updates.
omb_quote_short: supported by an independent reviewer within the agency who has not been involved in the development
notes: Peer review exists under the Directive (outside the questionnaire), so it is not counted. consultedTeams is not independent review.

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): named risk acceptance
aia_summary: No AIA question records a named individual who signs to accept residual risk.
nist_quote_short: Negative residual risks (defined as the sum of all unmitigated risks) to both downstream acquirers of AI systems and end users are documented.
omb_quote_short: risk acceptance, supported by a signature from the individual accepting the risk.
notes: ADMresponsible names an accountable official, but the AIA does not ask that person to accept documented residual risk.

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): cost analysis
aia_summary: No AIA question asks for direct costs and expected savings.
omb_quote_short: related costs analysis, supported by a summary of direct costs associated and expected savings, if any
notes: businessDrivers6A-6D cover benefits and performance, not costs. NIST MAP 3.2 is about the costs of AI errors, not budget, so it is not mapped.

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): reassessment schedule and significant modification
aia_summary: The AIA has a change log and retraining/review questions, but no question setting a reassessment schedule or reassessment after significant modification.
nist_quote_short: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes are planned
omb_quote_short: reassessment requirements following significant modifications to an underlying AI system
notes: The Directive requires the AIA to be updated when functionality or scope changes; that requirement sits outside the questionnaire.

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): opt-out of AI in favour of a human alternative
aia_summary: No AIA question gives affected individuals a choice to opt out of automated processing.
omb_quote_short: when possible, individuals who may interact with the AI have the ability to opt into and out of participating in the pilot
notes: This corrects the obvious mapping. M-25-21 has no general opt-out or human-alternative practice for high-impact AI; that practice was in the rescinded M-24-10. The only opt-in/opt-out text in M-25-21 is a condition for exempting pilot programmes. NIST AI RMF 1.0 has no opt-out subcategory either. aboutSystem9 (fallback when the system is unavailable) and riskProfile3 (populations excluded by design) are not opt-outs. So the gap exists on both sides; it is not a US practice missing from the AIA.

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): waivers, high-impact determinations and their publication
aia_summary: No AIA equivalent to recorded determinations that a presumed high-impact use is not high-impact, or to waivers of minimum practices and their public summaries.
omb_quote_short: each agency must publicly release a summary describing each individual determination and waiver, as well its justification
notes: The AIA has no waiver mechanism; its impact level is computed. The quote keeps the source wording "as well its justification".

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): termination of non-compliant AI and decommissioning
aia_summary: No AIA question on stopping a non-compliant system or on safe decommissioning.
nist_quote_short: Processes and procedures are in place for decommissioning and phasing out AI systems safely
omb_quote_short: the agency must safely discontinue use of the AI functionality

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): incident response and communication
aia_summary: No AIA question on incident identification, response or communicating errors to affected communities.
nist_quote_short: Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant AI actors, including affected communities.
notes: M-25-21 has no explicit incident-reporting practice for use cases, so the OMB column is blank.

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): organisational risk tolerance
aia_summary: The AIA computes an impact level but never asks the institution to state its risk tolerance.
nist_quote_short: Organizational risk tolerances are determined and documented.

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): third-party and pre-trained model monitoring
aia_summary: The AIA records who built the system but does not ask how third-party components or pre-trained models are monitored.
nist_quote_short: Pre-trained models which are used for development are monitored as part of AI system regular monitoring and maintenance.
notes: Vendor duties are in M-25-22 (out of scope).

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): diverse, interdisciplinary team
aia_summary: The AIA asks which teams were consulted on the AIA, not whether decisions about risk are made by a diverse, interdisciplinary team.
nist_quote_short: Decision-making related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks throughout the lifecycle is informed by a diverse team

aia_section: GAP (US practice, no direct AIA question): TEVV documentation
aia_summary: No AIA question asks for test sets, metrics and tools to be documented, or for test methods to be evaluated.
nist_quote_short: Test sets, metrics, and details about the tools used during TEVV are documented.
notes: fairnessDesign18A asks for metrics only in the narrower context of bias mitigation.

aia_section: GAP (AIA item, no US counterpart): accessibility standard and disability barriers
aia_summary: Conformance with CAN/ASC EN 301 549 and an assessment of barriers for persons with disabilities.
notes: Neither NIST AI RMF 1.0 nor M-25-21 has an accessibility requirement for AI systems. NIST mentions accessibility only in discussion text, not in a subcategory. US Section 508 obligations exist outside both documents. Disability performance testing (impact19I) is mapped in the subgroup performance row.
